outcome: maternal complications (emergency cesarean section, atony, chorioamnionitis)
cohort: 213 low-risk women with premature rupture of membranes (PROM) at >=37 weeks of gestation.
finding: Extending the latent phase to 24 hours in carefully selected PROM cases may offer a clinically meaningful, though not statistically significant, reduction in cesarean sections without increasing maternal or neonatal risks.
mod_finding: The 24-hour latent phase group showed a clinically relevant but non-significant 32% reduction in cesarean section rates compared to the 12-hour group.
